premises.opening: In the cinema, a ball flies out of the screen and Arjun ducks, spilling his popcorn
premises.question: How does a flat screen make a ball fly out at you?
premises.relevance: Everyone has felt a 3D movie reach out of the screen; few know their own eyes and brain do it
premises.motivation: Arjun just ducked from something that was never there and wants to know why
premises.discovery: Each eye gets its own picture through a filter, and the brain combines the two images into depth
premises.misunderstanding: The glasses have tiny screens inside them
premises.key_fact: The brain combines the two images into a single 3D view with depth
premises.demo: Glasses on, close one eye: the ball goes flat (eye views), then the projector and the filtering lenses
premises.payoff: Back in the cinema, Arjun knows the ball is two pictures and his brain, and he still ducks
premises.risks: Closing one eye removes stereoscopic depth, not every depth cue: say the pop-out goes flat, not that the world becomes 2D

premises.opening: After the movie Arjun says the 3D glasses must contain tiny screens
premises.question: What do 3D glasses actually do?
premises.relevance: A common wrong idea about an everyday object
premises.motivation: Arjun wants to prove his theory
premises.discovery: Each lens is a filter that lets only its own picture through
premises.key_fact: Each eye receives only the image with the matching polarization
premises.demo: Projector, screen and the two lenses
premises.payoff: The glasses are filters; the 3D happens in the brain
